title: A Reduced Carbohydrate Diet Intervention for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
brief_summary: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 5-10% of women of reproductive age, and is associated with infertility, risk for obesity and type 2 diabetes, and impaired quality of life. The elevated insulin characteristic of PCOS is likely to play a major role in its symptoms. Manipulation of dietary carbohydrate quantity and quality (glycemic load; GL) may lower insulin and improve both reproductive and metabolic outcomes. The purpose of this study is to determine if a lower GL diet intervention is more effective than a standard (STD) diet in improving reproductive and metabolic outcomes of women with PCOS in the absence of weight loss.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosed with PCOS
* Body mass index 18.5-35 kg/m2

Exclusion Criteria:

* Cushing's syndrome
* Type 1 or 2 diabetes
* Self-reported claustrophobia
* Androgenic tumors or adrenal hyperplasia
* Hyperprolactinemia
* Implanted metal items
* Use of metformin or other diabetes drug
* Women using oral contraceptives will not be excluded, but will be required to discontinue use of these agents 3 months prior to testing.
